{"id": "2:30/q11", "question": "Which angels were addressed?", "turns_on": "Whether the unqualified plural means every angel or the earthly company associated with Iblis.", "positions": [{"id": "2:30/q11/p1", "position": "The earthly angels were addressed", "reasons": "THALABI (author): The angels addressed here were those who had been on earth. BAGHAWI-FULL (author): The angels addressed were those who had lived on earth after God settled angels in heaven and jinn on earth; the jinn later became envious, rebellious, corrupt, and murderous. RAZI-FULL (author): A report gives successive tenfold ratios from humans and jinn through land, bird, and sea animals to earthly angels and the angels of each heaven, up to the angels of the Throne's pavilion; even all those angels are a drop beside those circling the Throne. BAYDAWI-FULL (الحكماء): In the philosophers’ account, the second class manages affairs from heaven to earth as divinely decreed; they include celestial and earthly angels. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (ابن مسعود وابن عباس): One view identifies the khalifa as Adam, succeeding earthly angels, the jinn, Iblis in earthly rule, or God; Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās are cited for the last view. ALUSI-FULL (author): The second group manages affairs from heaven to earth according to the prior decree; they obey commands and include heavenly and earthly angels, whose number only God knows. ALUSI-FULL (قيل): Another view limits the address to earthly angels because the discussion concerns vicegerency on earth. ALUSI-FULL (الخواص): Al-Khawwāṣ's account says earthly angels can err and places Iblīs among them at the Emerald Mountain near the eastern equator; al-Ālūsī says this would make earthly objection conceivable, God forbid."}, {"id": "2:30/q11/p2", "position": "All angels were addressed", "reasons": "IBNATIYYA-FULL (author): Angels do not know the unseen or speak ahead of God; the statement that they do not precede Him in speech praises all angels and indicates this is universal. TABRISI (author): God announces to the angels that He will create Adam as a successor on earth; the address may be to all angels or to those settled on earth after the jinn, per Ibn Abbas. RAZI-FULL (الأكثرون من الصحابة والتابعين): Most Companions and Successors say God addressed all angels: the unqualified term denotes them all, and restriction is contrary to the default. BAYDAWI-FULL (author): The unqualified address includes all angels; alternatives limit it to angels of earth or to Iblis and his angelic company, who were sent to defeat corrupting jinn that had first inhabited earth. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): The apparent reading makes the angels general; another group takes them specifically as earthly angels after the jinn or as those who fought with Iblis. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): If the angels addressed are all angels, the statement exposes Iblis's pride and reveals what God already knew; reports are cited from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī through his teachers. ELMALILI (author): These accounts exceed contemporary astronomy; subtle ether bodies cannot explain all angels, at most earthly and lowest-heaven angels unless the lowest heaven is narrowly construed, unlike theologians’ preferred view.
